subject: Dynamic reserve rebalancing for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@stratuslabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stratus Labs Procurement <procurement@stratuslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity request ahead of renewal -- usage spike context

Hi Ben,

Quick note from Stratus: over the last six weeks we've seen sustained double-digit growth in inference throughput from a new feature we soft-launched. Our internal ops pulled a utilization extract (attached) and it looks like our average GPU utilization is above 78% across peak windows, with frequent queueing at the 95th percentile.

Renewal is coming up in early September and procurement asked whether we can:
- add a modest number of GPUs to our Dedicated pool (initial ask: +8 A100-equivalents)
- keep the commit term the same but shift some capacity into a short-term burst/reserve pool during peak months

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a temporary reserve tranche with predictable pricing so we don't risk throttling during the next month? Also please advise if the utilization CSV is enough for you to make recommendations or if you need more telemetry (latency distributions, batch sizes).

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of ML Ops
Stratus Labs

Attachment: 2027-07-utilization-stratus.csv (CSV, 142 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity request ahead of renewal -- usage spike context

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the data, that CSV is helpful. Short answer: yes, we can provision an interim reserve tranche and convert to a permanent top-up at renewal if you’d like. Initial thoughts after a quick pass:

- Rather than +8 fixed GPUs, we recommend a 6-GPU steady add to the Dedicated pool plus a 4-GPU burst reserve that can be spun up for scheduled peak windows. This lowers baseline cost while preserving headroom.
- Pricing: propose a monthly reserved rate for the steady +6, and a utility billing model for the burst tranche (discounted incremental rate while reserved). I’ll have legal/finance numbers in the formal proposal.
- Technical ask for Karthik: can you validate the customer's batch distribution and advise on whether quantization or a small KV cache tweak will shave token cost?

Next steps: I’ll draft a short proposal (PDF) and a DocuSign for the amendment. Laura — can you pull the pricing/commit flavor for STR-2027-RNW-042 and confirm SLA for burst attach/detach windows? Karthik — can you review the attached CSV and add a short ops note?

Emily — I’ll loop back by Wednesday EOD with concrete numbers.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-initial-ask-notes.txt (text, 2 KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@stratuslabs.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity request ahead of renewal -- usage spike context

Ben / Emily —

I pulled the CSV and ran a quick profile against the model shard patterns Stratus is running. Notes:

- Peak windows show median sequence length increase (~1.4x) which explains higher token compute per request.
- Current batching looks conservative; increasing dynamic batch target by 15% for requests in the 50–95 ms latency bucket should improve throughput without bumping p95 beyond current SLA in our tests.
- Recommendation: enable a small prefix KV cache (per-route) and add quantized 8-bit variant for background burst instances — this reduces per-token cost ~12% during sustained burst periods.

Operationally, the reserve tranche we propose can be automated with our policy: attach within 10 minutes of threshold crossing and drain within 30 minutes after the window. For procurement/legal: this behavior is supported by an amendment (we can include runbook SLOs).

I’ll add a short Ops Annex to the PDF proposal with these parameters.

— Karthik
Principal Infra SWE | Redwood Inference

All —

Pricing & commercial summary for STR-2027-RNW-042:

- Steady add: +6 A100-eq GPUs as a 12-month addendum at the current committed unit price (no change to term).
- Burst reserve: +4 A100-eq GPUs as a month-to-month reserve with a utility billing discount of 25% off the on-demand incremental rate while attached. Reserve attach window policy per Karthik's note (10/30 minutes).
- Amendment: includes Ops Annex (Karthik) + one-week notice for scheduled attach for larger events.
- Estimated impact: +18% monthly commit cost; effective blended cost increase ~11% after factoring burst utility discount and expected burst duty cycle.

Emily — if that commercial structure works, we will deliver a one-page amendment + DocuSign. Please confirm procurement contact and whether Stratus needs an internal PO before signature.

Thanks,
